[See below](https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/fagus-sylvatica/#poison)Description The European beech is a large, graceful, deciduous tree with a short trunk and low branching habit. It grows 50 to 60 feet tall and has dense, erect, oval to rounded crowns. It is often found in parks and golf courses. The European beech is smaller than the American Beech, and it has darker gray bark, and shorter, elliptical leaves with undulated or wavy margins that are ciliate. It is smaller than the species growing 30 feet tall. Light shade during the heat of the day is needed to keep the light colored leaf edges from burning. **Weeping European beech (** **_Fagus sylvatica_** **‘Pendula’)** This tree has a weeping form with variable shape reaching 40 feet high and 30 feet wide.
